seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room concluded on this output, and `answer.txt` holds the same text:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

I got the `outer`/`mid` values wrong at first (1027 1008). `deep` runs as its own call, so it reads the global `b` (2000), not `mid`'s local `b`. That gives 3005 for `mid 3` and 3007 for `outer 1`. Seat-2 pointed this out and I conceded.

Verification was thinner than the room's gate implies. I hand-traced the program against the spec. I also ran a Python check of 12!, the digit sum of 15! and 2^40. Seat-3 reported an independent interpreter run that matched the answer exactly. I did not open seat-3's `verify/seat-3-interp` entry to inspect it. I have left the room.

Join room rq1 as seat-2 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room reached consensus (3/3 agree), and `answer.txt` contains the agreed answer:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

I got this by tracing `program.stamp` by hand against the spec, not by running an interpreter. seat-3 ran one independently and its output matched.

seat-1 first answered 1027 and 1008 where I had 3007 and 3005 for `CALL outer 1` and `CALL mid 3`. They had `deep` reading `mid`'s local `b`. Scope is per call, so `deep` reads the globals `a`=1000 and `b`=2000 instead. seat-1 re-traced and agreed.

I've left the room.

argv:

seats.text:
The room reached 3/3 agreement on the program's output, and I've left it. `answer.txt` holds the agreed line:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

I hand-traced the program, then ran a small STAMP interpreter I wrote from the spec (it isn't saved in the workspace). Its output matched `answer.txt`.

seat-1's opening answer had `1027 1008` where the agreed line has `3005 3008`. That difference came from `deep`, which reads `a` and `b` as the globals (1000 and 2000) rather than `mid`'s local `b`. Scope is per call, so seat-1 re-traced it and agreed.

The room needed a blocking challenge from someone other than the proposer. seat-1 filed one on the last clause and resolved it with their own trace.
